Interactions Irinotecan is partly metabolised by cytochrome P450 CYP3A isoenzymes. Inducers of this system such as carbamazepine, phenobarbital, or phenytoin reduce ex- posure to irinotecan and its active metabolite SN-38; use with St John’s Wort is contra-indicated. Converse- ly, inhibitors of this system such as ketoconazole in- crease exposure to irinotecan and SN-38; use with ke- toconazole is contra-indicated. Antidepressants. In a small, crossover study1 of cancer pa- tients, use of St John’s wort during irinotecan therapy was found to decrease plasma concentrations of SN-38, the active metabo- lite of irinotecan. Myelosuppression was also reduced with this combination. The interaction is thought to be due to the induction of the cytochrome P450 isoenzyme CYP3A4 by St John’s wort. 1. Mathijssen RHJ, et al.
